clinician.final_diagnosis: superior Foville syndrome due to a pontine hemorrhage
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old patient presented with abrupt onset left-sided weakness following headaches and vertigo. On admission, neurological examination revealed right oculomotor paralysis, right facial palsy, and left hemiparesis sparing the face, consistent with superior Foville syndrome. Brain CT imaging demonstrated a spontaneous hemorrhage in the right posterolateral pons compressing the fourth ventricle, confirming pontine hemorrhage as the etiology. The patient was treated with analgesics, anxiolytics, laxatives, and physiotherapy, showing clinical improvement and was discharged after 10 days.
